short: This entry holds the HMG-box factors that are neither SOX nor TCF/LEF: HMG20A (iBRAF), HMG20B (BRAF35) and BBX (bobby sox homolog). They share only the fold. HMG20A and HMG20B are paralogous subunits of chromatin complexes - HMG20B of the LSD1-CoREST-HDAC complex that keeps neuronal genes off in non-neuronal cells, HMG20A of KMT2A/MLL complexes that turn them on - so their genomic distribution is largely set by whichever partner recruits the complex. BBX is a poorly characterized protein that groups phylogenetically with CIC rather than with SOX. The three measured motifs are unrelated to each other and to the SOX core, and this is the least coherent family in the HMG class; a hit here should be treated as a lead, not an identification.
long:
## The factors

Three proteins are collected here, and what they have in common is a single HMG box, not a site.
HMG20B, originally named BRAF35 (BRCA2-associated factor 35), is a core subunit of the BHC
complex that pairs LSD1 (KDM1A) and CoREST with histone deacetylases and represses neuronal
genes in non-neuronal cells. HMG20A, its paralogue, was named iBRAF for inhibitor of BRAF35: it
opposes that complex and instead recruits KMT2A/MLL to drive neuronal gene expression, and it is
also found in a KMT2A-associated PHF5A-PHF14-HMG20A-RAI1 subcomplex. HMG20B has a separate
mitotic function that depends on its interaction with the BRC repeats of BRCA2. Both are broadly
expressed. BBX is a larger, much less studied protein, broadly expressed with enrichment in the
central nervous system, which phylogenetic analysis places with CIC (capicua) in an HMG-box
subfamily distinct from both SOX and TCF/LEF. The important structural point is that most HMG
boxes are architectural rather than sequence-reading domains: the HMGB1/HMGB2 type binds and
bends DNA with little sequence preference, and only a minority of the superfamily - SOX,
TCF/LEF, CIC and a few others - has demonstrable sequence specificity. Nothing published
establishes that HMG20A or HMG20B selects a specific sequence in cells.

## The motif

There is no single consensus for this family, which is why none is given. The four models here
disagree with each other; cohesion is 0.45, the lowest of the HMG-class families. BBX gives the
most informative model, and it is the family medoid: CIS-BP reports TGAACRVCGTTCA (15.1 bits)
and the Vierstra archetype AC0363 independently reports TGAACRNYGTTCA (15.8 bits). These are the
same 13-base element - an inverted repeat, since TGAAC and GTTCA are reverse complements, with
three variable bases between them. The half-site resembles the TGAAT half of the dimeric,
palindromic sites that appear in SOX models (Vierstra TGAATGTGCAGTCA, HOCOMOCO SOX1
TGAATANCATTCAT), differing at one position, which is consistent with BBX reading DNA in the same
general way as other sequence-specific HMG boxes. HMG20A's single HOCOMOCO model,
HM20A.H14CORE.0.SB.A, reads TCCCTAGGC (11.5 bits); its fourth field carries S, so it rests on
HT-SELEX rather than on ChIP, and it is graded A. CCTAGG is itself palindromic but bears no
relation to the SOX or TCF/LEF core. The HMG20B model, CIS-BP M02487_2.00, is ATTATAT (10.5
bits) and is inferred from the mouse protein at 94% DNA-binding-domain identity; a short AT-rich
string of this kind is what a non-sequence-specific HMG box tends to produce in a selection
experiment, and it should not be read as a recognition sequence.

## Where it acts

For HMG20A and HMG20B the practical answer is: wherever the complex goes. LSD1-CoREST-HDAC is
recruited to neuronal gene promoters largely by REST binding its own RE1/NRSE element, and KMT2A
complexes are recruited by their own targeting subunits; HMG20A and HMG20B come along as
subunits. Locations reported for them therefore track partner occupancy - neuronal gene
promoters, pancreatic islet regulatory regions where HMG20A is required for beta cell
maturation, adipocyte loci where HMG20A acts through MEF2C, and KMT2A targets in pancreatic
cancer stem cells. BBX has been mapped less. Its 13-base palindrome is specific by the standards
of this atlas: with two degenerate inner positions, TGAACRVCGTTCA is expected only a few hundred
times in a 3.1 Gb genome, against tens of thousands for the nine-base HMG20A model and millions
for a bare six-base HMG core.

## Biology and disease

HMG20B is required for repression of the neuronal program in non-neuronal cells and for
completion of mitosis, and its splicing has been implicated in breast cancer; the HMG20A locus
is a genome-wide-association signal for type 2 diabetes, and HMG20A is needed for functional
maturity of pancreatic beta cells, restrains adipogenesis through MEF2C, and supports the stem-
cell state in pancreatic cancer. The HMG20A/HMG20B antagonism is a clean example of two
paralogues with the same DNA-binding domain having opposite effects by virtue of the complexes
they join. BBX has been linked to phosphate homeostasis through regulation of FGF23 in bone, and
is maternally expressed and CNS-enriched in zebrafish and mouse. None of the three has an
established monogenic human disease.

## Reading a hit

Treat this family as a fold, not a motif: the models do not resemble one another and the family
cohesion is 0.45. The BBX palindrome is worth taking seriously as a sequence - two databases
derived it independently and it is long enough to be rare - but the label rests on in vitro
selection with no structural or functional follow-up, so "BBX site" is provisional, and because
the half-sites resemble those of dimeric SOX sites you should exclude SOX before settling on
BBX. An HMG20A match does not license the conclusion that HMG20A occupies the site: the HT-SELEX
evidence supports "this protein can bind this sequence", while in cells HMG20A is a passenger in
LSD1-CoREST and KMT2A complexes whose distribution is set by REST and other partners, so check
for an RE1/NRSE element nearby. The HMG20B model is mouse-inferred and low in information; do
not use it to call sites. More generally, a weak AT-rich match labelled with an HMG-box protein
is more likely to reflect a shape preference than a recognition sequence.
caveats: Low confidence throughout. This is a fold-defined group with no shared consensus and the lowest cohesion in the HMG class (0.45) across only four models. The BBX 13-base palindrome is reproduced by two databases and is rare enough to be useful, but rests on in vitro selection alone and its half-sites overlap those of dimeric SOX sites. The HMG20A motif has HT-SELEX support, yet HMG20A acts as a subunit of LSD1-CoREST and KMT2A complexes, so genomic locations attributed to it may belong to REST or another recruiting factor. The HMG20B model is inferred from mouse at 94% DNA-binding-domain identity and is an uninformative AT-rich string.
